- An India-focused Reddit discussion describes concern about babies falling on **granite, marble, or tile floors**; commenters discuss mats, carpets, and the practical difficulty of preventing every fall. ([parentcircle.com](https://www.parentcircle.com/how-to-keep-safe-my-child-89234/community-discussion))
- Public discussions also indicate that parents may see childproofing as a **time/installation burden** or prefer supervision and moving objects temporarily. This is anecdotal and mostly non-India-specific; it should be treated as a possible objection, not a market-wide finding. ([reddit.com](https://www.reddit.com/r/beyondthebump/comments/zdw2cr?utm_source=openai))

### 3. Safety guidance relevant to message claims

- The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission states that child-safety devices can reduce injury risk when correctly installed, but **no device is completely childproof** and supervision remains necessary. ([cpsc.gov](https://www.cpsc.gov/safety-education/safety-guides/kids-and-babies/Childproofing-Your-Home))
- Its guidance supports the general relevance of cabinet locks, corner/edge bumpers, outlet covers, door locks, and safety gates. It also highlights hazards not visibly covered by this kit, including furniture tip-over, windows/balconies, cords, stairs, pools, smoke alarms, and carbon monoxide. ([cpsc.gov](https://www.cpsc.gov/safety-education/safety-guides/kids-and-babies/Childproofing-Your-Home))
- Therefore, follow-up messages should avoid claims such as “your child is fully safe,” “accidents will be prevented,” or “this protects the entire home.” Safer framing is “helps reduce access to common reachable hazards.”

3. **Trust/risk reduction:** Mention the guarantee only with a clear link to eligibility and exclusions.
4. **Educational nudge:** Offer a short “six areas to check in your home” checklist, avoiding fear-based injury imagery.
5. **Indian-home relevance:** Use the brand’s own “designed for Indian homes” positioning, but avoid unsupported generalizations about all Indian homes.
6. **Urgency:** Use stock or delivery urgency only after resolving the homepage inconsistency.

{
  "answer_markdown": "## Abandoned-visitor follow-up sequence

Use only for visitors who have given the required consent for that channel. Do not send the same person the full sequence across WhatsApp, SMS and email. Stop all reminders after purchase, refund request or opt-out.

### 1) Product-page visitor — email or WhatsApp
**Send:** 2–4 hours after the visit

**Subject:** Still planning to childproof your home?

**Message:**
> Hi {{first_name}},
>
> If you were comparing ways to make your home easier to navigate with a curious little one, here’s a quick reminder of what’s inside The Peach Bucket 6-in-1 Child Safety Kit:
>
> • Edge and corner protectors  
> • Socket guards  
> • Cabinet and fridge locks  
> • Door guards  
>
> One organised kit for common, reachable hazards around the home—without needing a separate product for every area.
>
> It is designed for DIY setup, and one-to-one installation video guidance is available if you need help. Childproofing supports supervision; it does not make a home completely accident-proof.
>
> **View the kit:** https://thepeachbucket.com/products/the-peach-bucket-6-in-1-child-safety-kit
>
> — Team The Peach Bucket

### 2) Product-page visitor — educational follow-up
**Send:** 24 hours later, only if they did not purchase

**Subject:** A quick 6-area childproofing check

**Message:**
> Before your little one starts exploring, you may want to check these six areas:
>
> 1. Sharp edges and corners  
> 2. Easily reachable electrical sockets  
> 3. Cabinets and drawers  
> 4. Fridge or other accessible appliances  
> 5. Doors that can pinch little fingers  
> 6. Other hazards such as stairs, windows, balconies, cords and furniture that could tip
>
> The Peach Bucket kit is made for the first five areas above. It is not a substitute for supervision or for addressing hazards outside the kit’s coverage.
>
> **See what is included:** https://thepeachbucket.com/products/the-peach-bucket-6-in-1-child-safety-kit

### 3) Cart abandonment — email or WhatsApp
**Send:** 1–2 hours after cart abandonment

**Subject:** Your child-safety kit is still in your cart

**Message:**
> Hi {{first_name}},
>
> You left The Peach Bucket 6-in-1 Child Safety Kit in your cart.
>
> If the hesitation is installation, the kit is intended for DIY setup and one-to-one installation video support is advertised by the brand. If the hesitation is what it covers, it includes protection for edges, corners, sockets, cabinets/fridges and doors.
>
> **Return to your cart:** {{cart_url}}
>
> Please check the product details and compatibility with your home before ordering.

### 4) Checkout abandonment — email or WhatsApp
**Send:** 6–12 hours after checkout abandonment

**Subject:** Need help completing your order?

**Message:**
> Hi {{first_name}},
>
> Your order was not completed. If you had a question about delivery, payment, what is included, or installation, reply to this message and our team can help.
>
> You can continue here: {{checkout_url}}
>
> If the ₹299 prepaid saving is currently available for your order, it will be shown at checkout. Please rely on the amount displayed there rather than this reminder.

### 5) Final reminder
**Send:** 48 hours after the last message; do not use urgency

**Subject:** Keeping this here for you

**Message:**
> Hi {{first_name}},
>
> We’ll stop reminders after this message. If you still want to review The Peach Bucket 6-in-1 Child Safety Kit, you can find the details here:
>
> https://thepeachbucket.com/products/the-peach-bucket-6-in-1-child-safety-kit
>
> Choose childproofing products based on the areas in your home, correct installation and ongoing supervision. Reply if you need help understanding what the kit covers.

## Implementation checks before sending
